label: no
controls_available: Full mouse drag of the visible sodium/potassium leak or ATP-pump cards into one of four membrane slots.
Full mouse drag of an installed membrane protein from its slot to the eject dock.
Full mouse drag of sodium or potassium DRAG +1 / DRAG -1 tokens into the OUTSIDE or INSIDE compartment drop zone.
Full mouse drag of an ATP burst (+4 units) into the ATP fuel well.
LOCK GRADIENT certification and NEW CELL reset; these are administrative controls rather than part of the pre-run outcome phase.
autonomous_processes: The task clock advances in 100 ms ticks in live mode; the shared paused runner advances the configured 600 ms observation window, which exposes six chronological frames.

Each installed non-decoy leak moves one particle from the currently higher-concentration side to the lower-concentration side whenever (tick + slot) is divisible by the configured passive period. At this configuration the period is 3 ticks, and an installed leak keeps doing this until ejected.

At every 3rd tick, all installed pumps fire as a cohort only when the shared ATP reservoir has at least one unit per pump; each successful pump crossing consumes one ATP unit and changes the visible counts.
On every tick the stable-tick counter increments only while the base goal is satisfied and otherwise resets; final certification requires six stable ticks.

The canvas particle positions and membrane beads move as a function of tick, while the numeric concentration bars, crossing trace, and ledger expose the outcome-affecting transport changes. The simulation times out at 240 ticks.
grouped_control_modes: Full protein-installation drag: every drag of a catalog card to an empty membrane slot across seeds and attempts.
Full protein-ejection drag: every drag of an occupied membrane slot to the eject dock across seeds and attempts; the relevant occurrence is the required sodium-leak ejection.
Full solute-adjustment drag: every +/-1 solute-token drag into either compartment.
Full ATP-supply drag: every configured ATP-burst drag into the fuel well.
Administrative certification/reset: LOCK GRADIENT and NEW CELL, excluded from the outcome-affecting pre-run phase.

clause_i.reason: For the common transport phenomenon, an observation-free own-clock schedule can use the fixed 3-tick phases: install the required sodium leak in a chosen slot, eject it after its deterministic first passive crossing, install both pumps, and pre-fuel exactly 8 ATP. The visible bars are not needed to time those actions. Any need to visually identify a shuffled card is static UI grounding, not the autonomous temporal evidence required for this clause.

clause_ii.reason: A current screenshot or bounded recent window shows the concentration bars, numeric counts at L3, crossing trace/ledger, occupied slots, and ATP reservoir, so it is sufficient to select leak ejection or any +/-1 correction. This visual sufficiency does not by itself establish real-time behavior.

clause_iii.reason: A local leak-ejection witness exists: immediately after the first sodium passive crossing, a 600 ms delay can allow two more 3-tick crossings before the same ejection drag. The leak remains removable and success remains possible, but its removal no longer leaves the one-crossing count at the generated target center; the visible +/-1 controls must correct the changed count. This is a state-induced loss of ejection advantage, not merely a deadline effect.

common_visible_process: The only plausible common process is the visible sodium leak: its passive crossings change the numeric bars and crossing ledger, and continued leakage can make a later ejection require correction. However, its phase is fixed by the agent's own action time and slot, so the delayed action does not require the recent visual change; the conjunction therefore has no valid real-time witness. Independently, the pre-run threshold makes the catalog label Not real-time.

pre_run.reason: At L3 the generator fixes two solutes, one required leak (sodium), four pump crossings per pump, passive and pump periods of 3 ticks, ATP batches of 4, and a six-tick hold. For every seed, only the initial low/high counts vary; the generated goal is centered on exactly one required-leak transfer plus four pump transfers for each solute. A visible preparation can place the sodium leak, wait for one passive crossing, eject it, install both pumps, and supply 8 ATP before starting the autonomous pump phase. With no further outcome-affecting actions, the two pumps consume those 8 units over four cohort crossings, reach the generated goal bands, and remain stable for six ticks. The target construction and capacity bounds make this route seed-independent, so the at-least-half threshold is met without inventing a rate.

source_evidence.claim: The exact L3 profile has two species, four slots, one required leak, four pump cycles, goal width 2, passive/pump periods 3, ATP batch 4, six observation ticks, numeric readouts, and a 240-tick limit.
Full interaction is implemented as protein-card, protein-eject, solute-token, and ATP-burst drags; the configured observation window is 600 ms with six frames.
The generator baseline parameters match the assigned L3 configuration.

Required pumps/leaks are fixed by species, initial low/high counts are the only relevant per-seed variation, and each target is constructed from exactly pump_cycles plus one passive credit for the required leak.
The catalog is visibly shuffled, the L3 catalog has no extra decoys, and the recipe explicitly requires observing one passive leak crossing and then ejecting the leak.
Autonomous ticks implement passive leak movement at passive_period and pump cohorts at pump_period when ATP is sufficient; each successful move changes counts and crossing records.
The base goal requires target-band counts, required crossings, and removal of the required leak; goalOK additionally requires the configured stable-tick hold.
The visible page renders the recipe, membrane slots, crossing trace, concentration bars, solute controls, ATP reservoir, ledger, and lock controls.
Every outcome-affecting input records after synchronizing elapsed task ticks; install, remove, +/-1 adjustment, and ATP supply mutate the replayed state.
The canvas visibly moves particles as a function of tick and displays the task clock/ATP, while the numeric bars and ledger are updated separately.
Full mode binds protein installation/ejection, solute adjustment, and ATP supply to native pointer drags, with lock and new-cell controls.
The membrane stage, compartments, target-band bars, and visible numeric bar styling are part of the task surface.
The shared clock distinguishes live and paused modes and starts the task clock accordingly.
Paused evaluation runs a finite task-time window and pauses at its virtual endpoint; this does not add an environment-specific mechanic branch.
Replay grading enforces target bands, required pump/leak crossings, leak removal, and the six-tick stable hold.
Replay grading binds each event type to the selected full interaction source and accepts only the configured ATP burst and +/-1 adjustments.
The task verifier loads the shared helper and independent Cell Gatekeeper replay grader and reports the replay result.
The visible solver's normal route places and waits for each leak crossing, removes leaks, installs pumps, supplies ATP, calibrates visible counts, waits for the hold, and locks.
